prerequisites: Proficiency in the theory of differential equations
Knowledge acquired in the Theory of Machines course
Knowledge acquired in the Technology of Machines course

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of vibration and noise in machines.
Understand the origin and effects of noise and vibrations in machines.
Apply noise and vibration measurement techniques in machines.
Apply techniques for reducing noise and vibration emissions according to regulations.
Assess the impact of noise and vibrations on humans and the environment.

syllabus_topics: Free vibrations without damping in single degree of freedom systems
Free vibrations with damping in single degree of freedom systems
Forced vibrations in single degree of freedom systems
Equation of motion in systems with n degrees of freedom
Specific case for a two degrees of freedom system
Dynamic model of the human body
Introduction to vibrations in machines and applications
Acoustic propagation: Free field and diffuse
Environmental standards and legislation on noise
assessment_rules: To pass without Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC), a minimum exam score of 5 (out of 10) is required. To add the PEC score to the final grade, a minimum exam score of 4 (out of 10) is required. PECs are optional, but not doing them means renouncing continuous assessment. The maximum grade can only be obtained by completing both the personal exam and the PEC. For extraordinary calls (e.g., September), the same grading criteria apply, but the PEC is only offered in May. Approved laboratory practices are valid for five years.
